subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: Narrow bedroom, bed close to the wall: here is how the door decision gets made, one step at a time.
ig:
Narrow bedroom, bed close to the wall: here is how the door decision gets made, one step at a time.

This is the sequence we follow when a fitted wardrobe has to share a tight room with a bed:

1. Measure the gap between wardrobe wall and bed.
2. Test the swing. A sheet of cardboard cut to door width tells you more than any drawing.
3. List what you store, from long coats to shoes.
4. Choose the doors. In a typical narrow room, sliding doors win because they need no swing space.
5. Plan the interior around the overlap, so drawers never catch.
6. Fit and set the tracks level, so the doors run smoothly.

It is the same thinking whether the room is a box room in Biddulph or the main bedroom in a new build.

Try step two this weekend and you will know your answer. Share this with whoever you are planning the bedroom with.
fb:
Here is a trick worth trying before you decide between sliding and hinged wardrobe doors: cut a sheet of cardboard to the width of a door and swing it out from the wall. If it hits the bed, or leaves you squeezing past, you have your answer.

That is step two of the six we go through when planning a wardrobe for a narrow bedroom. The rest covers what you store, the door choice, planning drawers around the sliding overlap, and setting the tracks level on fitting day.

alt: Six-frame sequence: measuring the gap to a bed, a cardboard swing test, a storage list, sliding doors in a narrow bedroom, an interior plan and tracks being levelled.
on_asset: F1: Measure the gap — The distance from the wardrobe wall to the bed decides whether a hinged door can swing open fully, or would hit the bed. | F2: Test the swing — A sheet of cardboard cut to door width shows how much room a hinged door really takes before anything is built. | F3: List what you store — Long coats, shirts, folded jumpers, shoes. The mix decides how much hanging, shelving and drawer space each section needs. | F4: Choose the doors — In a typical narrow room, sliding doors win: no swing space needed, at the cost of seeing part of the wardrobe at a time. | F5: Plan around the overlap — Drawers sit fully within one door opening, with hanging space where the doors overlap, so nothing catches. | F6: Fit and set level — Tracks are set level on fitting day and the doors adjusted so they run smoothly and meet evenly. | Label on photo frames: Concept image
